construct.rationale: The protein has 659 residues, above the provider limit of 400. Residue 525 lies in the UniProt domain Protein kinase (402-655); the construct is that domain with up to 10 flanking residues on each side.

superposition.method: Least-squares rigid-body fit (Kabsch) of the variant model onto the reference model
superposition.scope: C-alpha atoms of the 240 residues with pLDDT of at least 70 in both models

local_difference.scope: C-alpha atoms within 8 angstroms of the C-alpha of residue 525 in the reference model, the site included

contacts.exclusion: The residues bonded to the site in sequence (positions -1 and +1) are left out.
contacts.label: computed from predicted model

masking.rule: A residue is masked when either model has pLDDT below 70 there. Masked residues carry no displacement.

caveats.text: Structure predictors are not validated for single-residue substitutions. A variant model that matches the reference carries no information about whether the variant is tolerated. Differences smaller than run-to-run variation are noise. See the evidence panel for functional, curated, population and predictor data.

caveats.text: AlphaFold has not been validated for predicting the effect of mutations. In particular, AlphaFold is not expected to produce an unfolded protein structure given a sequence containing a destabilising point mutation.
caveats.quoted_from: AlphaFold DB FAQ. Helix applies the same caveat to every structure predictor.

caveats.text: A predictor producing a similar fold for the variant sequence is expected for most single substitutions and is uninformative about stability.
pLDDT is each model's own confidence estimate. The two values at the site are model behaviour, never measured destabilisation. Low pLDDT means disorder or insufficient information.
Distances, contacts and displacements are geometry computed from predicted models, not observations of the protein.
This model is deterministic: there is no seed and one model per sequence, so run-to-run variation is not estimated and no noise baseline is available for these differences.
Both models cover a residue window, not the full-length protein. Contacts with the rest of the chain, with partners and with ligands are absent from both.
